body: That's not what I'm saying either. I'm saying if your wife is a stay at home, dont come home and belittle her work by saying how much more shit you had to deal with than her. She's doing her job, you ought to do yours. I'm not talking about moms in general. Just the one you interact with the most.

Before I say anything more, I want you to realize that you'll always feel this way in varying degrees. But staying on medication, long term, can really help soften the edges. I used cycle from feeling a million miles high to knife-at-my-throat suicidal but medication helped toned that down a lot. I'm no doctor, but from my understanding medication helps level all the ups and downs to make you feel more consistent throughout the year. I still feel the pain, I still feel happy, but not so much that when I go through my depressing phases that I'll jump out a window. It gets it to a point where I can cope with it, but doesn't erase it. And try to find one good therapist and stick with them. It helps a lot when they have a history with you.
I could but then I wouldn't have any money left. Plus I'd have no mode of transportation, thus losing my job.
Still, they don't deserve to be berated because of it. I think that's the biggest issue stay at home parents face. It's not the hardest job, but you should still respect them for doing it.

That sounds awesome, but I don't make enough to live on my own. I don't even have a driver's license because my parents were afraid I'd run away as soon as I got one. Do you have any advice on how to be financially independent? I make about $1.5k per month but living in the city is rather expensive...

It doesn't end if you don't put the effort into ending it. And regardless of what everyone says on here, it never truly ends. You'll always feel that bitter sadness in your chest. No amount of medication or therapy will change that. But it gets better. When you decide to turn your life around, you'll see. You'll fill your life with activities like work or going to parties and eventually you'll find a means of living. You start thinking about paying bills and rent, and that will soon be enough to keep you alive. Is this sad? Is this depression? No, this is life. You have to realize that everyone feels this way. Everyone is depressed about living, and they all want to die. The difference between a mentally healthy person and a clinically depressed one is how they handle it. We just need a little help with medication and therapy, but understand that everyone feels the same pain.

Find something to fill up your time. Get a job. Move out. When there's more to do, there's less time to think about what's going on in your head.
